name: Juliet's House, Verona
name_zh: 维罗纳 · 朱丽叶之家
prototype_of: 莎士比亚《罗密欧与朱丽叶》里“美丽的维罗纳”那座阳台的化身：这座 13 世纪的老宅属于卡佩罗家族，名字很像剧中的凯普莱特家，20 世纪 30 年代市政府给它加装了一座石阳台，从此成了全世界恋人的朝圣地。院子里有朱丽叶铜像，墙上贴满情书和纸条，“朱丽叶俱乐部”的志愿者至今还在替她回信
prototype_of_en: The real-world stand-in for the balcony in 'fair Verona' of Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet. This thirteenth-century house belonged to the Cappello family, a name close to the play's Capulets, and in the 1930s the city added a stone balcony to it; it has been a pilgrimage site for lovers ever since. There's a bronze Juliet in the courtyard, the walls are covered in love notes, and volunteers of the Juliet Club still answer the letters people write to her

name: Casa di Dante, Florence
name_zh: 佛罗伦萨 · 但丁故居
note: 但丁 1265 年出生在佛罗伦萨这片窄巷里，九岁时第一次见到贝雅特丽齐，后来把这份爱写成了诗文集《新生》。1302 年他被政敌判处流放，再没回过故乡，《神曲》就是在流亡中写成的。这座塔楼式的“但丁之家”是 20 世纪初按中世纪样子重建的纪念馆，附近的小教堂据说是他第一次见到贝雅特丽齐的地方
note_en: Dante was born in 1265 in these narrow streets of Florence and first saw Beatrice when he was nine, a love he later turned into the Vita Nuova. In 1302 his political enemies sentenced him to exile and he never came home again, writing the Divine Comedy as an exile. This tower-house, the Casa di Dante, is a museum rebuilt in medieval style in the early twentieth century, and the little church nearby is said to be where he first saw Beatrice

name: Basilica of Santa Croce, Florence
name_zh: 佛罗伦萨 · 圣十字教堂
note: 《看得见风景的房间》里，英国姑娘露西被同行的老小姐丢在圣十字教堂，手里没了旅游指南，只好自己看乔托的壁画，在这里遇见了不按规矩说话的乔治父子，一段爱情由此开始。这座教堂里葬着米开朗基罗、伽利略和马基雅维利，还有但丁的纪念墓。司汤达就是在这里看画看得心跳加速、头晕目眩，“司汤达综合征”由此得名
note_en: In A Room with a View, Lucy Honeychurch is abandoned in Santa Croce by her companion without her Baedeker and has to look at the Giotto frescoes on her own, and here she meets the unconventional Emersons, father and son, and the love story begins. Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli are buried in the church, and Dante has a memorial here. It was here, too, that Stendhal was so overwhelmed by the art that his heart raced and his head swam, giving its name to 'Stendhal syndrome'

name: Parco di Pinocchio, Collodi
name_zh: 科洛迪 · 匹诺曹公园
note: 《木偶奇遇记》的作者卡洛·洛伦齐尼小时候常来母亲的家乡科洛迪村，后来就用这个村名做了笔名。这座 1956 年开放的匹诺曹公园沿着林间小路摆着书里的场景：会说话的蟋蟀、狐狸和猫、红虾酒馆、吞下匹诺曹和杰佩托的大鲨鱼，孩子们可以钻进鲨鱼肚子里。山坡上就是老村子和加尔佐尼别墅的花园
note_en: Carlo Lorenzini, author of Pinocchio, spent childhood stays in Collodi, his mother's home village, and later took its name as his pen name. This park, opened in 1956, lines a woodland path with scenes from the book: the Talking Cricket, the Fox and the Cat, the Red Lobster Inn, and the great shark that swallows Pinocchio and Geppetto, which children can climb inside. The old village and the gardens of Villa Garzoni are on the hill above

name: Dante's Tomb, Ravenna
name_zh: 拉文纳 · 但丁墓
note: 被佛罗伦萨流放的但丁在拉文纳度过最后几年，在这里写完《神曲》天堂篇，1321 年死于这座城市。佛罗伦萨几百年来一再讨要遗骨，拉文纳的方济各会修士干脆把骨头藏了起来，直到 1865 年才被重新发现。墓前有一盏长明灯，灯油至今由佛罗伦萨每年送来，算是迟到的赔罪
note_en: Exiled from Florence, Dante spent his last years in Ravenna, finished the Paradiso here and died in the city in 1321. For centuries Florence kept demanding his bones back, so the Franciscan friars of Ravenna simply hid them, and they weren't found again until 1865. A lamp burns before the tomb, and to this day Florence sends the oil for it every year, a belated apology

name: Keats-Shelley House, Rome
name_zh: 罗马 · 济慈-雪莱故居
note: 1820 年，患肺结核的济慈来罗马养病，就住在西班牙阶梯旁这座粉色房子的二楼，第二年 2 月死在这里，年仅二十五岁。他的墓在城南的新教徒公墓，墓碑上只刻着“这里躺着一个名字写在水上的人”。故居现在是纪念济慈、雪莱和拜伦的博物馆，从他的窗口就能看见阶梯和破船喷泉
note_en: In 1820 John Keats, ill with tuberculosis, came to Rome hoping to recover and took rooms on the second floor of this pink house beside the Spanish Steps; he died here the following February, aged twenty-five. He is buried in the Protestant Cemetery in the south of the city, under a stone that reads only 'Here lies One Whose Name was writ in Water'. The house is now a museum of Keats, Shelley and Byron, and from his window you can see the steps and the Barcaccia fountain

name: Fountain of the Four Rivers, Piazza Navona, Rome
name_zh: 罗马 · 纳沃纳广场四河喷泉
note: 《天使与魔鬼》里，兰登教授沿着贝尼尼雕塑组成的“光明之路”在罗马城里追凶，第四个“元素”——水——就落在纳沃纳广场贝尼尼的四河喷泉：凶手要把一位枢机主教活活沉进池里，兰登跳进水里搏斗。喷泉的四尊巨像代表多瑙河、恒河、尼罗河和拉普拉塔河，广场原本是古罗马的赛场，所以是长椭圆形的
note_en: In Angels & Demons, Robert Langdon chases a killer across Rome along a 'Path of Illumination' marked by Bernini's sculptures, and the fourth element, water, brings him to Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers in Piazza Navona, where the killer is drowning a cardinal and Langdon dives in to fight him. The four giant figures stand for the Danube, Ganges, Nile and Río de la Plata, and the square is long and oval because it was once an ancient Roman stadium

name: Rione Luzzatti, Naples
name_zh: 那不勒斯 · 卢扎蒂区
prototype_of: 那不勒斯四部曲里莉拉和埃莱娜长大的那个“城区”的原型：东边铁路旁这片 20 世纪 20 年代建的工人住宅区，费兰特在书里没有点名，读者从隧道、铁路和教堂认出了它。第一部里两个女孩从这里穿过隧道去看海；最后一部《失踪的孩子》里，莉拉四岁的女儿蒂娜就在这片街上不见了。这里至今是普通居民区，去时保持低调
prototype_of_en: The model for the 'neighborhood' where Lila and Elena grow up in the Neapolitan Novels: a 1920s working-class housing estate beside the railway on the east side of Naples. Ferrante never names it, but readers have recognized it from the tunnel, the railway and the church. In the first book the girls set off through the tunnel from here to see the sea; in the last, The Story of the Lost Child, Lila's four-year-old daughter Tina vanishes from these streets. It's still an ordinary residential district, so keep a low profile
coord_checked: San Giuseppe Maggiore dei Falegnami (Napoli) (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:San_Giuseppe_Maggiore_dei_Falegnami_(Napoli)

name: Forum, Pompeii
name_zh: 庞贝 · 广场
note: 布尔沃-利顿 1834 年的《庞贝城的末日》让维苏威火山埋掉的这座城市家喻户晓：盲眼卖花女尼迪亚在火山灰和黑暗中凭着熟悉的街道领着恋人逃生。他说庞贝是“那个时代文明的缩影”，一座让众神藏起来留给后世惊叹的玩具城。马克·吐温在《傻子出国记》里也写过在这些石板路上走、看车辙的感受。广场是古城的中心，北面远远能望见维苏威火山
note_en: Edward Bulwer-Lytton's The Last Days of Pompeii (1834) made the city buried by Vesuvius known to everyone: in the ash and darkness the blind flower-girl Nydia, who knows the streets by heart, leads the lovers to safety. He calls Pompeii 'the miniature of the civilization of that age', a toy city the gods hid away for posterity to marvel at. Mark Twain writes in The Innocents Abroad about walking these paving stones and tracing the chariot ruts. The forum was the center of the town, with Vesuvius rising in the distance to the north

name: Ponte Azzone Visconti, Lecco
name_zh: 莱科 · 阿佐内·维斯孔蒂桥
note: 意大利人人读过的《约婚夫妇》开篇第一句就写这里：“科莫湖向南伸出的那一支……”，湖面收窄成河，一座古桥标出湖的尽头和阿达河的开始——说的就是这座 14 世纪的石桥。年轻的伦佐和露琪亚就住在莱科附近的村子，一个恶霸贵族不准他们成婚，故事由此开始。曼佐尼在莱科度过童年，他家的别墅现在是博物馆
note_en: The Betrothed, the novel every Italian reads at school, opens right here: 'That branch of the Lake of Como which turns toward the south…', where the lake narrows into a river and an old bridge marks the point where the lake ends and the Adda begins; that's this fourteenth-century stone bridge. Young Renzo and Lucia live in a village near Lecco, and the story begins when a bullying nobleman forbids their wedding. Manzoni spent his childhood in Lecco, and his family's villa is now a museum

name: Sacra di San Michele
name_zh: 圣米迦勒修道院
prototype_of: 《玫瑰的名字》里那座山顶修道院的灵感来源之一：埃科写 1327 年一位方济各会修士和他的徒弟在一座意大利北部的本笃会修道院里调查一连串离奇死亡，人们普遍认为这座矗立在苏萨谷口千米岩峰上的千年修道院给了他灵感。从山脚沿古道爬上去，要穿过一道陡峭的“死者阶梯”，顶上能俯瞰整个阿尔卑斯山前的平原
prototype_of_en: One of the inspirations for the mountaintop abbey in The Name of the Rose. Eco's novel follows a Franciscan friar and his novice investigating a string of strange deaths at a Benedictine abbey in northern Italy in 1327, and this thousand-year-old abbey on a rock a thousand meters above the mouth of the Susa valley is widely taken to have inspired it. Climb the old path from below and you pass up the steep 'Stairway of the Dead' to a view over the whole plain at the foot of the Alps

name: Castel del Monte
name_zh: 蒙特城堡
prototype_of: 《玫瑰的名字》里那座八角形塔楼的藏书楼的原型之一：小说里修道院的“楼堡”四角各有一座七边形塔楼，藏着迷宫般的图书馆，常被认为是参照了这座腓特烈二世 13 世纪建在普利亚山顶的八角城堡。城堡本身八边形、八座八角塔、每层八个房间，用途至今说不清，是世界遗产，印在意大利一欧分硬币上
prototype_of_en: One of the models for the octagon-towered library building in The Name of the Rose. The abbey's Aedificium in the novel, with a tower at each corner and a labyrinthine library inside, is often said to draw on this octagonal castle built by Frederick II on a hilltop in Apulia in the thirteenth century. The castle itself has eight sides, eight octagonal towers and eight rooms on each floor, and nobody is quite sure what it was for; it's a World Heritage Site and appears on the Italian one-cent coin

name: Aliano
name_zh: 阿利亚诺
note: 1935 年，反法西斯的医生、画家卡洛·莱维被墨索里尼流放到巴西利卡塔这座悬在白色泥岩沟壑上的山村，在这里住了一年，后来写成《基督停在埃博利》：书名是农民的说法，意思是连基督都没走到这么远，文明和国家都把他们遗忘了。书里村子叫“加里亚诺”，就是阿利亚诺。莱维的故居和文学公园都在，他按遗愿葬在了村里的墓地
note_en: In 1935 the anti-Fascist doctor and painter Carlo Levi was banished by Mussolini to this Basilicata village perched above ravines of white clay, and spent a year here; it became Christ Stopped at Eboli, a title taken from the peasants' saying that even Christ never came this far, that civilization and the state had forgotten them. The book calls the village Gagliano, and it is Aliano. You can visit Levi's house and a literary park, and he is buried in the village cemetery, as he wished

name: Rossano
name_zh: 罗萨诺
note: 英国作家诺曼·道格拉斯 1911 年前后徒步走遍卡拉布里亚，写成《古老的卡拉布里亚》，书里这座山城的窗外是“红土峡谷、橄榄树和绿松石色的伊奥尼亚海”，远处就是古希腊的锡巴里斯平原。罗萨诺的大教堂供奉着“非人手所画”的圣母像，主教博物馆里藏着 6 世纪的紫色福音书，是世界上最古老的插图福音书之一
note_en: The English writer Norman Douglas walked the length of Calabria around 1911 and wrote it up as Old Calabria; from his room in this hill town he looked down 'a many-folded gorge of glowing red earth' to the turquoise Ionian Sea, with the plain of ancient Sybaris beyond. Rossano's cathedral keeps an image of the Virgin said to be 'painted by no human hand', and the diocesan museum holds the sixth-century Purple Codex, one of the oldest illustrated Gospels in the world

name: Bastione di Saint Remy, Cagliari
name_zh: 卡利亚里 · 圣雷米棱堡
note: 1921 年 1 月，D. H. 劳伦斯和妻子从西西里坐船来到撒丁岛，只待了九天，就写出了《大海与撒丁岛》。船靠近时，他看见卡利亚里“赤裸裸地陡然升起，金灿灿的，一直堆到天上”，像中世纪手抄本里的耶路撒冷。上岸后他爬上的那片“悬在城市上空”的大平台，就是这座圣雷米棱堡，从这里能看到港口、盐湖和海
note_en: In January 1921 D. H. Lawrence and his wife took the boat from Sicily to Sardinia, stayed just nine days, and he wrote Sea and Sardinia. As the ship came in he saw Cagliari as 'a naked town rising steep, steep, golden-looking, piled naked to the sky', like Jerusalem in an illuminated missal. The great terrace he climbed to after landing, 'curiously suspended over the town', is this bastion of Saint Remy, with the harbor, the salt lagoons and the sea spread out below

name: Punta Secca (Montalbano's house)
name_zh: 蓬塔塞卡 · 蒙塔巴诺的家
prototype_of: 卡米莱里笔下蒙塔巴诺探长住的海边小镇“马里内拉”在电视剧里的样子：小说从《水的形状》开始，写西西里虚构小城维加塔的警长蒙塔巴诺破案、吃海鲜、清早在家门口的海里游泳。电视剧把他的家拍在蓬塔塞卡灯塔旁这座带露台的海滨小楼，从此成了粉丝必到之地，现在是一家民宿。附近的拉古萨、希克利一带也都是剧中的维加塔
prototype_of_en: What Marinella, the seaside village where Andrea Camilleri's Inspector Montalbano lives, looks like on screen. Starting with The Shape of Water, the novels follow Montalbano in the invented Sicilian town of Vigàta as he solves crimes, eats seafood and swims in the sea outside his front door every morning. The TV series filmed his house in this beach house with a terrace next to the Punta Secca lighthouse, and fans have flocked here ever since; it's now a B&B. Nearby Ragusa and Scicli stand in for Vigàta itself

name: Palazzo Doria-Tursi, Genoa
name_zh: 热那亚 · 多利亚-图尔西宫
note: 马克·吐温 1867 年坐游轮来欧洲，写成《傻子出国记》。在热那亚，一位导游兴奋地给他们看哥伦布的亲笔信和半身像，一行美国人故意装傻，一遍遍问“哥伦布？他……他死了吗？”，把导游急得跳脚——这是书里最有名的笑话之一。市政厅所在的这座宫殿今天仍陈列着哥伦布的书信，还有帕格尼尼的小提琴
note_en: Mark Twain came to Europe on a cruise ship in 1867 and wrote The Innocents Abroad. In Genoa an excited guide shows the Americans a letter in Columbus's own hand and a bust of him, and they play dumb, asking again and again, 'Christopher Colombo… is he dead?', until the guide is beside himself; it's one of the most famous jokes in the book. This palace, Genoa's town hall, still displays Columbus's letters, along with Paganini's violin

name: Palazzo Leopardi, Recanati
name_zh: 雷卡纳蒂 · 莱奥帕尔迪故居
note: 莱奥帕尔迪 1798 年生在马尔凯山城雷卡纳蒂的这座贵族府邸里，在父亲两万册藏书的图书馆里埋头苦读，自学了希腊文和希伯来文，也读坏了身体。二十一岁那年他坐在家附近的小山上，一道树篱挡住了远方的地平线，写下意大利最著名的短诗《无限》。府邸里的图书馆至今开放，那座小山就叫“无限之丘”
note_en: Giacomo Leopardi was born in 1798 in this noble house in the hill town of Recanati in the Marche, and buried himself in his father's library of twenty thousand books, teaching himself Greek and Hebrew and ruining his health. At twenty-one, sitting on a little hill near the house where a hedge blocked out the distant horizon, he wrote 'The Infinite', the most famous short poem in Italian. The family library is still open to visitors, and the little hill is called the Colle dell'Infinito

name: Monument to Ovid, Sulmona
name_zh: 苏尔莫纳 · 奥维德像
note: 《变形记》的作者奥维德公元前 43 年出生在阿布鲁佐山间的苏尔莫纳，后来被奥古斯都流放到黑海边，再没回来。他在流放中写诗说：“苏尔莫纳是我的故乡，清冽的泉水最丰沛”，城里至今把这句话的缩写 SMPE 刻在城徽上。市中心广场上立着他的铜像，这里还以彩色的糖衣杏仁闻名
note_en: Ovid, author of the Metamorphoses, was born in 43 BC in Sulmona, in the mountains of Abruzzo; the emperor Augustus later banished him to the Black Sea, and he never came back. In exile he wrote 'Sulmo is my homeland, richest in ice-cold streams', and the town still carries the abbreviation SMPE on its coat of arms. His bronze statue stands in the main square, and the town is also famous for its colorful sugared almonds

name: Basilica of San Francesco, Assisi
name_zh: 阿西西 · 圣方济各大殿
note: 圣方济各 1182 年生在翁布里亚的阿西西，放弃家产做了托钵修士。14 世纪的《圣方济各的小花》收集了他和弟兄们的故事：向鸟儿讲道、驯服古比奥的狼、在风雪路上讲什么是“完全的喜乐”，几百年来是意大利最受欢迎的宗教读物之一。他死后两年人们就为他建了这座上下两层的大殿，乔托画的方济各生平壁画就在上教堂里
note_en: St Francis was born in Assisi in Umbria in 1182 and gave up his family's wealth to become a mendicant friar. The fourteenth-century Little Flowers of St Francis gathers stories of him and his brothers, preaching to the birds, taming the wolf of Gubbio, explaining on a snowy road what 'perfect joy' is, and it has been one of the best-loved religious books in Italy for centuries. This two-level basilica was begun two years after his death, and the Giotto frescoes of his life are in the Upper Church

name: Harbor, Riva del Garda
name_zh: 加尔达湖畔里瓦 · 港口
note: 1909 和 1913 年卡夫卡两次来加尔达湖北岸的里瓦度假疗养，后来写了短篇《猎人格拉胡斯》：一艘挂着黑帆的小船驶进里瓦的小港，船上躺着一个死了几百年、却永远到不了冥界的猎人。卡夫卡的故事里很少出现真实的地名，这是难得的一个。港口边那座方形的阿波纳莱钟楼至今还在，湖上的帆船和当年一样多
note_en: Franz Kafka came to Riva on the northern shore of Lake Garda for holidays and rest cures in 1909 and 1913, and later wrote the short story 'The Hunter Gracchus', in which a boat with dark sails glides into Riva's little harbor carrying a hunter who died centuries ago and can never reach the land of the dead. Real place names are rare in Kafka, and this is one of them. The square Apponale tower still stands over the harbor, and the lake is as full of sailboats as ever

name: Tower of the Leper, Aosta
name_zh: 奥斯塔 · 麻风病人塔
note: 1811 年，萨伏依作家格扎维埃·德·梅斯特尔写了一个真实的故事：奥斯塔城墙边的一座古塔里，独居着一个被全城隔离的麻风病人，只有一个花园和他死去的妹妹的回忆陪着他，一位军官偶然闯进花园，两人聊了一个下午。这篇《奥斯塔城的麻风病人》在 19 世纪的欧洲感动了无数读者，古塔从此就叫“麻风病人塔”，至今立在城西
note_en: In 1811 the Savoyard writer Xavier de Maistre wrote up a true story: in an old tower on the walls of Aosta lived a leper, shut away from the whole town, with only a garden and memories of his dead sister for company, until an officer wandered into the garden one day and they talked for an afternoon. 'The Leper of the City of Aosta' moved readers all over nineteenth-century Europe, and the tower has been called the Tower of the Leper ever since; it still stands on the west side of town

name: Petrarch's House, Arquà Petrarca
name_zh: 阿尔夸彼特拉克 · 彼特拉克故居
note: 彼特拉克写给劳拉的三百多首诗编成《歌集》，给整个欧洲定下了十四行诗的样子。他晚年隐居在尤加内丘陵的这座小村，1374 年死在这里，村子后来干脆改名叫“阿尔夸彼特拉克”。故居保留着他的书房，还有一只据说是他养的猫的标本，他的墓就在教堂前的广场上
note_en: Petrarch's Canzoniere, more than three hundred poems mostly to Laura, set the pattern for the sonnet all over Europe. He spent his last years in this village in the Euganean Hills and died here in 1374, and the village later renamed itself Arquà Petrarca. The house keeps his study and a mummified cat said to have been his, and his tomb stands in the square in front of the church

name: Santa Maria Novella, Florence
name_zh: 佛罗伦萨 · 新圣母大殿
note: 《十日谈》的故事从这里开始：1348 年黑死病横扫佛罗伦萨，七位年轻女子在新圣母大殿做完弥撒，约上三位青年躲到城外的乡间别墅，十天里每人每天讲一个故事，一共一百个。教堂的大理石立面出自阿尔贝蒂之手，里面有马萨乔的《三位一体》和乔托画的十字架
note_en: The Decameron begins here: in 1348, as the Black Death sweeps through Florence, seven young women meet after Mass in Santa Maria Novella and, joined by three young men, escape to villas outside the city, where each tells a story a day for ten days, a hundred in all. The marble façade is by Alberti, and inside are Masaccio's Trinity and a crucifix painted by Giotto

name: House of Ludovico Ariosto, Ferrara
name_zh: 费拉拉 · 阿里奥斯托故居
note: 阿里奥斯托为费拉拉的埃斯特家族写了《疯狂的罗兰》：骑士为爱发疯，阿斯托尔福骑着鹰头马飞上月亮替罗兰找回理智，是文艺复兴最受欢迎的长诗。晚年他用积蓄盖了这座小楼，门面上刻着拉丁文“小，但合我意”，1533 年死在这里，楼里是一座小纪念馆
note_en: Ariosto wrote Orlando Furioso for the Este court of Ferrara: knights driven mad by love, and Astolfo riding the hippogriff to the moon to fetch back Orlando's wits; it was the best-loved long poem of the Renaissance. Late in life he built this small house with his savings and had 'Small, but suited to me' carved in Latin on its front; he died here in 1533, and it is now a small museum

name: Sant'Onofrio al Gianicolo, Rome
name_zh: 罗马 · 贾尼科洛山圣奥诺弗里奥修道院
note: 塔索写十字军攻下耶路撒冷的《被解放的耶路撒冷》，一生被精神病和迫害妄想折磨，在费拉拉被关了七年。1595 年他住进贾尼科洛山上的这座修道院，等着教皇为他加冕桂冠诗人，没等到就死在了这里。教堂里有他的墓，附近公园里那棵“塔索橡树”的枯干还在
note_en: Tasso wrote Jerusalem Delivered, the epic of the crusaders taking Jerusalem, and was tormented all his life by mental illness and fears of persecution; Ferrara kept him locked up for seven years. In 1595 he moved into this monastery on the Janiculum to await his crowning as poet laureate by the pope, and died here before it could happen. His tomb is in the church, and the dead trunk of 'Tasso's oak' still stands in the park nearby

name: Monument to Virgil, Mantua
name_zh: 曼托瓦 · 维吉尔纪念碑
note: 维吉尔公元前 70 年生在曼托瓦附近，他在《埃涅阿斯纪》第十卷里专门写到故乡：这座城由女先知曼托的儿子建立，以母亲的名字命名。《神曲》里给但丁引路的维吉尔，开口也说自己的父母“都是曼托瓦人”。湖边的维吉尔广场上立着 1927 年落成的诗人像
note_en: Virgil was born near Mantua in 70 BC, and wrote his hometown into Book 10 of the Aeneid: a city founded by the son of the prophetess Manto and named after his mother. In Dante's Inferno, Virgil introduces himself the same way, saying that his parents were both Mantuans. His statue, unveiled in 1927, stands in the Piazza Virgiliana near the lakes

name: Castello di Colloredo di Monte Albano
name_zh: 科洛雷多城堡
note: 涅埃沃 1857 到 1858 年在母亲家族的科洛雷多城堡里，用八个多月写完了《一个意大利人的自白》：八十岁的卡尔洛回忆自己从威尼斯共和国覆灭到意大利统一的一生。三年后他乘船遇难，年仅二十九岁，没能看到书出版。城堡在 1976 年弗留利地震中严重损毁，近年才修复
note_en: In 1857–58 Nievo wrote Confessions of an Italian in a little over eight months at Colloredo, the castle of his mother's family: the eighty-year-old Carlo looks back on a life that runs from the fall of the Venetian Republic to the unification of Italy. Three years later Nievo was lost at sea at twenty-nine and never saw the book published. The castle was badly damaged in the Friuli earthquake of 1976 and has been restored in recent years
coord_checked: Castello di Colloredo di Monte Albano (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Castello_di_Colloredo_di_Monte_Albano

name: Aci Trezza
name_zh: 阿奇特雷扎
note: 维尔加的《马拉沃利亚一家》写的就是卡塔尼亚北边这个渔村：一家渔民押上全部家当，赊了一船羽扇豆去卖，船却在风暴里沉了，从此家道败落。海里那几块黑色的火山岩叫“独眼巨人礁”，传说是独眼巨人朝奥德修斯扔的石头。村里有一座以小说命名的“枇杷树之家”小纪念馆
note_en: Verga's The House by the Medlar Tree is set in this fishing village north of Catania: a family of fishermen stake everything on a cargo of lupins bought on credit, the boat goes down in a storm, and their long decline begins. The black volcanic stacks offshore, the Cyclopean Isles, are said to be the rocks the Cyclops hurled at Odysseus. The village has a small museum named after the novel, the Casa del Nespolo

name: Vizzini
name_zh: 维齐尼
note: 维尔加的家族来自卡塔尼亚内陆的山城维齐尼，《堂·杰苏阿尔多师傅》就以这里为背景：泥瓦匠出身的杰苏阿尔多拼命挣下家业，娶了没落贵族的女儿，却被贵族和穷亲戚两头看不起。小城的老街和贵族宅邸都还在，广场上有维尔加的雕像，他的《乡村骑士》也发生在这一带
note_en: Verga's family came from Vizzini, a hill town inland from Catania, and Mastro-don Gesualdo is set here: Gesualdo, a mason who scrapes together a fortune and marries the daughter of a fallen noble house, is looked down on by the gentry and his poor relations alike. The old streets and noble houses are still there, with a statue of Verga, and his 'Cavalleria rusticana' is set around here too

name: Palazzo Zuccari, Rome
name_zh: 罗马 · 祖卡里宫
note: 邓南遮的《欢乐》写 19 世纪末罗马的唯美派贵族安德烈亚·斯佩雷利，他就住在西班牙阶梯顶上的祖卡里宫，在两个女人之间周旋。这座 16 世纪画家祖卡里给自己盖的房子，最出名的是格雷戈里亚纳街那面张着怪兽大嘴的门窗。今天这里是赫尔齐亚纳艺术史图书馆
note_en: D'Annunzio's The Child of Pleasure follows Andrea Sperelli, an aesthete aristocrat in late nineteenth-century Rome, who lives in Palazzo Zuccari at the top of the Spanish Steps and is torn between two women. The house the painter Federico Zuccari built for himself in the sixteenth century is famous for the monsters' gaping mouths that frame its door and windows on Via Gregoriana. It is now the Bibliotheca Hertziana, an art-history library

name: Casa Pascoli, Castelvecchio
name_zh: 卡斯泰尔韦基奥 · 帕斯科利故居
note: 帕斯科利少年时父亲被人杀害，家人又接连去世，他的诗里满是乡野的小东西：《柽柳集》写鸟、树篱、田间的活计和死去的亲人。1895 年起他和妹妹住在托斯卡纳山谷里的这座房子，后来的许多诗都写在这里。房子保持着他生前的样子，他就葬在家里的小礼拜堂
note_en: Pascoli's father was murdered when he was a boy and more family deaths followed; his poems are full of small country things, and Myricae is about birds, hedges, work in the fields and the family dead. From 1895 he lived with his sister in this house in a Tuscan valley and wrote much of his later poetry here. The house is kept as he left it, and he is buried in its chapel

name: Monastery of San Nicolò l'Arena, Catania
name_zh: 卡塔尼亚 · 圣尼科洛本笃会修道院
note: 德·罗伯托的《总督》写西班牙总督后裔乌泽达家族在意大利统一前后的贪婪和争产，家里的小儿子被送进卡塔尼亚的这座本笃会修道院，修士们过的是贵族般的奢华日子。这座欧洲最大的修道院之一现在是卡塔尼亚大学的人文学院，可以参观回廊和地下的古罗马遗迹
note_en: De Roberto's The Viceroys follows the greedy, quarrelling Uzeda family, descendants of the Spanish viceroys, through the years of Italian unification; younger sons are packed off to this Benedictine monastery in Catania, where the monks live like lords. One of the largest monasteries in Europe, it now houses the University of Catania's humanities department, and you can tour its cloisters and the Roman remains beneath
coord_checked: Monastero di San Nicolò l'Arena (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Monastero_di_San_Nicolò_l'Arena

name: Pirandello's birthplace, Caos, Agrigento
name_zh: 阿格里真托 · 皮兰德娄故居
note: 皮兰德娄 1867 年生在阿格里真托城外这片叫“混沌”的乡间，常说自己是“混沌之子”。《已故的帕斯卡尔》里被误认为已死、借机换个身份重活的男人，《六个寻找剧作家的角色》里闯进排练场的剧中人，都在追问“我是谁”。故居现在是博物馆，他的骨灰安放在屋旁的一块岩石里
note_en: Pirandello was born in 1867 in this stretch of country outside Agrigento called Caos, 'Chaos', and liked to call himself a son of Chaos. The man in The Late Mattia Pascal who is wrongly declared dead and seizes the chance to become someone else, and the characters in Six Characters in Search of an Author who burst in on a rehearsal, are all asking who they are. The house is a museum, and his ashes lie in a rock beside it
coord_checked: File:Casa natale di Pirandello.JPG (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Casa_natale_di_Pirandello.JPG

name: Statue of Italo Svevo, Trieste
name_zh: 的里雅斯特 · 斯韦沃铜像
note: 斯韦沃是的里雅斯特的商人，白天管岳父家的油漆厂，夜里写小说，前两部无人问津，直到他的英语老师乔伊斯把他推荐给法国评论家，《泽诺的意识》才走红：一个总也戒不掉烟的商人，听心理医生的话写下自己的一生。老城霍尔蒂斯广场上有他的铜像，脚下刻着书里的一句话
note_en: Svevo was a Trieste businessman who ran his in-laws' paint company by day and wrote at night; his first two novels went unnoticed until his English teacher, James Joyce, brought Zeno's Conscience to French critics: a businessman who can never quite give up smoking writes down his life on his psychoanalyst's orders. His bronze stands in Piazza Hortis in the old town, with a line from the novel set in the pavement at his feet
coord_checked: File:Italo Svevo at Piazza Hortis - panoramio.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Italo_Svevo_at_Piazza_Hortis_-_panoramio.jpg

name: Monterosso al Mare
name_zh: 五渔村 · 蒙特罗索
note: 蒙塔莱童年和青年时代的夏天都在五渔村的蒙特罗索度过，家里的别墅就在费吉纳海滩边。《乌贼骨》里灼热的岩石、龙舌兰、晒白的墙和拍岸的海，写的就是这段利古里亚海岸，他后来凭诗歌获得诺贝尔文学奖。镇上的小路边有刻着他诗句的石板
note_en: Montale spent the summers of his childhood and youth at Monterosso in the Cinque Terre, where his family's villa stood by Fegina beach. The burning rocks, agaves, sun-bleached walls and pounding sea of Cuttlefish Bones are this stretch of Ligurian coast, and he went on to win the Nobel Prize for his poetry. Stone tablets carved with his lines stand along the paths of the town

name: San Martino del Carso
name_zh: 圣马蒂诺德尔卡尔索
note: 一战时翁加雷蒂是卡尔索高原前线的步兵，在战壕里用铅笔把短诗写在明信片和纸片上，后来编成《欢乐集》。其中一首就叫《圣马蒂诺德尔卡尔索》，写这个被炮火夷平的村子只剩几截残墙，而他的心才是最残破的村庄。村边的翁加雷蒂公园里立着刻这首诗的石碑
note_en: In the First World War Ungaretti was an infantryman on the Carso front, pencilling short poems on postcards and scraps of paper in the trenches; they became L'Allegria. One of them is named after this village, flattened by the guns: only shreds of wall are left of its houses, he writes, but his heart is the most shattered village of all. A stone carved with the poem stands in the Parco Ungaretti by the village

name: Villa Buzzati, Belluno
name_zh: 贝卢诺 · 布扎蒂别墅
note: 布扎蒂 1906 年生在贝卢诺城外家族的这座别墅里，一辈子爱多洛米蒂山。《鞑靼人沙漠》里年轻军官德罗戈被派到边境要塞，一年又一年等着从北方沙漠来的敌人，等到老也没等来；那荒凉的群山里，有他故乡山影的影子。别墅至今属于布扎蒂家族
note_en: Buzzati was born in 1906 in his family's villa outside Belluno and loved the Dolomites all his life. In The Tartar Steppe the young officer Drogo is posted to a frontier fortress and waits year after year for an enemy from the northern desert who never comes, among bleak mountains that owe something to those of his home. The villa still belongs to the Buzzati family
coord_checked: File:Villa Buzzati a Belluno.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Villa_Buzzati_a_Belluno.jpg

name: Fossoli camp
name_zh: 福索利集中营
note: 1944 年初，作为游击队员被捕的普里莫·莱维被关进摩德纳附近的福索利中转营，2 月 22 日和六百多名犹太人一起被塞进闷罐车送往奥斯维辛。《这是不是个人》第一章就从这里的最后一夜写起。营地残存的营房正在修复，旁边卡尔皮城里有被驱逐者纪念馆
note_en: Early in 1944 Primo Levi, arrested as a partisan, was held in the Fossoli transit camp near Modena, and on 22 February he and some 650 Jews were loaded into freight cars for Auschwitz. The first chapter of If This Is a Man begins with the last night here. What remains of the barracks is being restored, and the Museum-Monument to the Deportee is in nearby Carpi

name: La Pigna, Sanremo
name_zh: 圣雷莫 · 皮尼亚老城
prototype_of: 《树上的男爵》里翁布罗萨的原型：十二岁的柯西莫赌气爬上树，从此一辈子没再落地，在树上读书、恋爱、帮山贼、见拿破仑。卡尔维诺在圣雷莫长大，书里那座临海的山城和连绵的树林，就是照着故乡的利古里亚海岸写的。皮尼亚老城的陡巷和过街拱至今像一座迷宫
prototype_of_en: The model for Ombrosa in The Baron in the Trees: at twelve, Cosimo climbs a tree in a sulk and never sets foot on the ground again, reading, falling in love, helping brigands and meeting Napoleon from the branches. Calvino grew up in Sanremo, and the hill town above the sea and the endless woods of the book are drawn from this Ligurian coast. The steep lanes and archways of the old Pigna quarter are still a maze

name: Lungomare Italo Calvino, Sanremo
name_zh: 圣雷莫 · 卡尔维诺海滨大道
note: 卡尔维诺两岁时随父母回到圣雷莫，在这座海滨小城一直长到二十出头。《马可瓦尔多》写的却是北方工业城市里的一个搬运工：他在水泥和霓虹灯之间寻找蘑菇、鸽子和一点点季节的痕迹，二十个故事正好走过五轮春夏秋冬。圣雷莫把港口边这段海滨大道命名为卡尔维诺大道
note_en: Calvino was brought to Sanremo at the age of two and grew up in this seaside town until his early twenties. Marcovaldo, though, is about a laborer in a northern industrial city who hunts for mushrooms, pigeons and any trace of the seasons among the concrete and neon; its twenty stories run through five rounds of spring, summer, autumn and winter. Sanremo has named this stretch of seafront by the harbor after him
coord_checked: File:Lungomare Italo Calvino - panoramio.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lungomare_Italo_Calvino_-_panoramio.jpg

name: Corte del Milion, Venice
name_zh: 威尼斯 · 百万宅院
note: 《看不见的城市》里，马可·波罗向忽必烈汗讲述他走过的五十五座奇异城市，可汗发现他一次也没提到威尼斯，波罗回答说，每次描述一座城市，他说的都是威尼斯。里亚尔托桥附近这座小院叫“百万宅院”，据说就是波罗家住过的地方，他的游记在意大利就叫《百万》
note_en: In Invisible Cities, Marco Polo describes fifty-five fantastic cities to Kublai Khan, and when the Khan points out that he has never once mentioned Venice, Polo answers that every time he describes a city he is saying something about Venice. This little courtyard near the Rialto is the Corte del Milion, where the Polo family is said to have lived; in Italian his book of travels is called Il Milione
coord_checked: File:Corte seconda del Milion e porticato del teatro Venezia.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Corte_seconda_del_Milion_e_porticato_del_teatro_Venezia.jpg

name: Procida
name_zh: 普罗奇达岛
note: 莫兰特的《阿图罗的岛》写少年阿图罗在那不勒斯湾的普罗奇达岛上野生野长，崇拜总是离家远行的父亲，直到父亲带回一个十六岁的新娘。岛顶那座古城堡改成的监狱，在书里一直投下阴影。科里切拉渔港的彩色房子层层叠叠，是岛上最美的一角
note_en: Morante's Arturo's Island is about a boy growing up wild on Procida in the Bay of Naples, worshipping a father who is always away, until the father brings home a sixteen-year-old bride. The old castle turned prison at the top of the island casts its shadow over the book. The stacked pastel houses of the fishing harbor of Corricella are the island's loveliest corner

name: San Lorenzo, Rome
name_zh: 罗马 · 圣洛伦佐区
note: 《历史》的主人公是罗马的小学女教师伊达，她带着被德国士兵强暴后生下的小儿子乌塞佩，在战争和饥饿里挣扎。1943 年 7 月 19 日盟军轰炸罗马，她住的圣洛伦佐工人区被炸成废墟。区里的圣洛伦佐城外大殿也在那天被炸，后来按原样修复
note_en: The heroine of History is Ida, a Roman schoolteacher struggling through war and hunger with Useppe, the little son born after a German soldier raped her. On 19 July 1943 Allied bombs fell on Rome and reduced her working-class neighborhood of San Lorenzo to rubble. The basilica of San Lorenzo fuori le Mura was hit the same day and was rebuilt as it had been
coord_checked: San Lorenzo fuori le mura (Rome) (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:San_Lorenzo_fuori_le_mura_(Rome)

name: Palazzo Filangeri-Cutò, Santa Margherita di Belice
name_zh: 圣玛格丽塔迪贝利切 · 菲兰杰里-库托宫
prototype_of: 《豹》里萨利纳亲王一家每年夏天去住的多纳富加塔府邸的原型：作者托马西·迪·兰佩杜萨小时候常在母亲家族的这座宫殿里度夏，晚年把这段记忆写进了小说。宫殿在 1968 年贝利切地震中几乎全毁，重建后成了市政厅和一座关于《豹》的文学博物馆
prototype_of_en: The model for Donnafugata, the palace where the Prince of Salina takes his family every summer in The Leopard: Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa spent childhood summers in this palace of his mother's family and put the memory into his novel late in life. It was almost destroyed in the Belice earthquake of 1968; rebuilt, it now houses the town hall and a literary museum devoted to the novel
coord_checked: Palazzo Filangeri-Cutò (Santa Margherita di Belice) (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Palazzo_Filangeri-Cutò_(Santa_Margherita_di_Belice)

name: Corso Ercole I d'Este, Ferrara
name_zh: 费拉拉 · 埃尔科莱一世大道
note: 巴萨尼的《芬齐-孔蒂尼花园》写 1938 年种族法颁布后的费拉拉：被赶出网球俱乐部的犹太青年们，聚到城墙边富有的芬齐-孔蒂尼家的大花园里打球、恋爱，几年后都被送进了集中营。这家人是虚构的，但书里那条通往城墙的林荫大道就是这条埃尔科莱一世大道
note_en: Bassani's The Garden of the Finzi-Continis is set in Ferrara after the racial laws of 1938: young Jews thrown out of the tennis club gather to play and fall in love in the great garden of the wealthy Finzi-Continis by the city walls, a few years before they are deported. The family is invented, but the avenue running out to the walls in the book is this Corso Ercole I d'Este

name: Villa Valguarnera, Bagheria
name_zh: 巴盖里亚 · 瓦尔瓜尔内拉别墅
prototype_of: 《玛丽安娜·乌克里亚漫长的一生》里那座别墅的原型：18 世纪的西西里贵族女子玛丽安娜幼年受惊后变得又聋又哑，十三岁嫁给自己的舅舅，靠读书和写字在沉默中活出了自己。马莱伊尼母亲的家族就是这座别墅的主人，玛丽安娜也真有其人，是她的祖先。别墅是私人宅邸
prototype_of_en: The model for the villa in The Silent Duchess: Marianna, an eighteenth-century Sicilian noblewoman left deaf and mute by a childhood shock and married at thirteen to her own uncle, makes a life of her own in silence through reading and writing. The villa belonged to Dacia Maraini's mother's family, and Marianna was a real ancestor of hers. It is a private house

name: Vecchiano
name_zh: 韦基亚诺
note: 塔布齐 1943 年生在比萨，在附近韦基亚诺乡下的外祖父母家长大，一辈子把这里当家。《佩雷拉的证词》写 1938 年萨拉查独裁下的里斯本，一个胖胖的老报人怎样一点点醒过来，这本书在意大利成了抗争的象征。他爱上葡萄牙，最后葬在里斯本，而这片松林小路是他童年的风景
note_en: Tabucchi was born in Pisa in 1943 and grew up at his grandparents' home in Vecchiano nearby, which he always treated as home. Pereira Maintains is set in Lisbon in 1938 under Salazar, where a stout old newspaperman slowly wakes up to the dictatorship, and in Italy the book became a byword for resistance. He fell in love with Portugal and is buried in Lisbon, but these pine-lined lanes were the landscape of his childhood

name: Palazzo Contarini Fasan, Venice
name_zh: 威尼斯 · 孔塔里尼-法桑宫（苔丝狄蒙娜之家）
prototype_of: 大运河边这座窄窄的哥特式小宫殿，几百年来被威尼斯人叫作“苔丝狄蒙娜之家”，当成《奥赛罗》里那位嫁给摩尔将军的元老之女的家。剧里她父亲勃拉班修半夜被叫醒，开口就是“这里是威尼斯，我家不是乡下农庄”。宫殿是私宅，从对岸或水上巴士上看最好
prototype_of_en: This narrow Gothic palazzo on the Grand Canal has been called 'Desdemona's House' by Venetians for centuries, the home of the senator's daughter in Othello who marries the Moorish general. When her father Brabantio is roused in the night in the play, his first retort is 'This is Venice. My house is not a grange.' It's a private house, best seen from the opposite bank or a vaporetto

name: Hotel des Bains, Lido di Venezia
name_zh: 威尼斯丽都岛 · 浴场大饭店
note: 1911 年托马斯·曼和妻子住进丽都岛这家海滨大饭店，在这里见到一个美丽的波兰少年，回去写了《死于威尼斯》：作家阿申巴赫住进同一家“浴场饭店”，迷上少年塔齐奥，霍乱在城里蔓延也不肯离开。维斯康蒂的同名电影也在这里拍摄。饭店 2010 年已歇业，只能从外面看
note_en: In 1911 Thomas Mann and his wife stayed at this grand seaside hotel on the Lido, where he saw a beautiful Polish boy, and he went home to write Death in Venice: the writer Aschenbach checks into the same 'Bäder-Hotel', becomes infatuated with the boy Tadzio and will not leave as cholera spreads through the city. Visconti filmed it here too. The hotel closed in 2010 and can only be seen from outside
coord_checked: Hotel des Bains (Lido di Venezia) (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Hotel_des_Bains_(Lido_di_Venezia)

name: Pianosa
name_zh: 皮亚诺萨岛
note: 海勒把《第二十二条军规》里美军轰炸机中队的基地放在托斯卡纳群岛的皮亚诺萨岛，又在书前说明这座岛其实小得装不下书里发生的事。他本人二战时驻扎在旁边的科西嘉岛，飞了六十次任务。这座平坦的小岛后来长期是重刑犯监狱，现在属于国家公园，限量乘船登岛
note_en: Heller put the bomber squadron of Catch-22 on Pianosa, in the Tuscan Archipelago, while noting at the front of the book that the island is far too small to hold everything that happens in it. He himself flew sixty missions from neighboring Corsica in the war. The flat little island was long a maximum-security prison and is now part of a national park, with a limited number of visitors allowed over by boat

name: Salone dei Cinquecento, Palazzo Vecchio, Florence
name_zh: 佛罗伦萨 · 维奇奥宫五百人大厅
note: 丹·布朗的《地狱》里，兰登在佛罗伦萨醒来，失去了记忆，追着但丁《地狱篇》留下的线索奔走，一条关键线索就藏在维奇奥宫五百人大厅瓦萨里的巨幅战争壁画里：一面小旗上写着“寻找就会发现”。这句字真的在画上，传说画后面还藏着达·芬奇失传的壁画
note_en: In Dan Brown's Inferno, Robert Langdon wakes up in Florence with no memory and chases clues hidden in Dante's Inferno; a key one is in Vasari's huge battle fresco in the Hall of the Five Hundred in Palazzo Vecchio, where a tiny flag reads 'cerca trova', seek and you shall find. The words really are in the painting, and legend says a lost mural by Leonardo lies behind it

name: Palazzo Barbaro, Venice
name_zh: 威尼斯 · 巴巴罗宫
prototype_of: 《鸽翼》里莱波雷利宫的原型：身患绝症的美国女继承人米莉租下大运河边的这座宫殿，在这里度过最后的日子，身边的人各怀心思等着她的遗产。亨利·詹姆斯多次住在朋友柯蒂斯一家的巴巴罗宫，萨金特、惠斯勒也是这里的常客。宫殿至今是私宅
prototype_of_en: The model for Palazzo Leporelli in The Wings of the Dove, where Milly Theale, a dying American heiress, spends her last days on the Grand Canal while those around her wait, each with designs on her fortune. Henry James stayed many times at Palazzo Barbaro with his friends the Curtises, whose guests also included Sargent and Whistler. It is still a private house
coord_checked: File:Palazzo Barbaro a San Vidal.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Palazzo_Barbaro_a_San_Vidal.jpg

name: Palazzo Soranzo Cappello, Venice
name_zh: 威尼斯 · 索兰佐-卡佩罗宫
prototype_of: 《阿斯彭文稿》里那座破旧宫殿的原型：一个美国编辑化名住进去，想从一位老小姐手里套出已故诗人阿斯彭的情书。詹姆斯写的是一条冷清小运河边带大花园的宫殿，一般认为原型就是这座索兰佐-卡佩罗宫，它的花园在威尼斯数一数二。现在是文物保护部门的办公楼
prototype_of_en: The model for the shabby palace in The Aspern Papers, where an American editor takes rooms under a false name, hoping to wheedle the dead poet Aspern's love letters out of an old lady. James describes a palace with a large garden on a quiet, melancholy canal, and it is generally taken to be this Palazzo Soranzo Cappello, whose garden is one of the largest in Venice. It now houses offices of the heritage authority

name: Estoul, Brusson
name_zh: 布鲁松 · 埃斯图尔
prototype_of: 《八座山》里格拉纳村的原型之一：城里男孩皮埃特罗每年夏天随父母来到罗莎峰下的小山村，和放牛娃布鲁诺成了一辈子的朋友，又跟着父亲一座座登上冰川。科涅蒂小时候的夏天就在布鲁松山上的埃斯图尔度过，后来常年住在阿尔卑斯山里写作。从村子往上能走到绿湖和阿尔普小屋
prototype_of_en: One of the models for Grana in The Eight Mountains: every summer Pietro, a city boy, comes with his parents to a little village below Monte Rosa, where he and Bruno, a cowherd, become friends for life, and his father leads him up one glacier after another. Cognetti spent the summers of his childhood at Estoul, above Brusson, and later went to live in the Alps to write. Paths from the village climb to the Lac Vert and the Arp hut

name: Monument to Edmondo De Amicis, Turin
name_zh: 都灵 · 德·亚米契斯纪念碑
note: 德·亚米契斯在都灵住了大半辈子，《爱的教育》就是都灵小学生安利柯三年级一整年的日记：班上来了卡拉布里亚的新同学，老师每月讲一个“每月故事”，比如《万里寻母》。都灵人在新门火车站前的桑布伊花园里给他立了这座纪念碑，碑座正面有他的浮雕头像
note_en: De Amicis lived most of his life in Turin, and Heart is the diary of Enrico, a Turin schoolboy, through one school year: a new boy arrives from Calabria, and each month the teacher reads a 'monthly story' such as 'From the Apennines to the Andes'. Turin put up this monument to him in the Giardino Sambuy in front of Porta Nuova station, with his portrait in relief on the front of the base
coord_checked: File:Monumento a Edmondo de Amicis (Edoardo Rubino 1914).jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Monumento_a_Edmondo_de_Amicis_(Edoardo_Rubino_1914).jpg

name: Galluras Museum, Luras
name_zh: 卢拉斯 · 加卢拉斯民俗博物馆
note: 《送终女人》写 50 年代撒丁岛的小村：六岁的玛丽亚被过继给裁缝老妇博纳利亚，后来才知道养母还是村里的“送终女人”，夜里去替痛苦不止的垂死者结束生命。加卢拉高原上卢拉斯镇的加卢拉斯民俗博物馆里，陈列着一把据说属于送终女人的木槌，是这个传说少见的实物
note_en: Accabadora is set in a Sardinian village in the 1950s: six-year-old Maria is adopted by Bonaria, an old seamstress, and only later learns that her new mother is also the village's accabadora, who goes out at night to end the lives of the dying who are suffering. The Galluras ethnographic museum in the town of Luras, in the Gallura hills, displays a wooden mallet said to have belonged to an accabadora, a rare physical trace of the tradition

name: Arsita
name_zh: 阿尔西塔
note: 迪·彼得兰托尼奥 1962 年生在阿布鲁佐大萨索山脚下的阿尔西塔，在山村长大，后来做了儿童牙医。《被归还的女孩》写 1975 年一个十三岁女孩突然被养父母送回从没见过的亲生家庭，一个贫穷的山村大家庭，书里的方言和乡下日子都来自她熟悉的这片山区
note_en: Di Pietrantonio was born in 1962 in Arsita, below the Gran Sasso in Abruzzo, grew up in the mountain countryside and became a children's dentist. A Girl Returned is about a thirteen-year-old who in 1975 is suddenly sent back by the couple who raised her to a birth family she has never known, a big, poor household in the hills; the dialect and country life of the book come from this part of Abruzzo she knows

name: Crema Cathedral
name_zh: 克雷马 · 大教堂广场
scene: 小说把故事放在八十年代意大利海边的一座别墅里，电影把时间定在 1983 年夏天，搬到伦巴第平原的小城克雷马拍摄：少年埃利奥和来家里做客的美国学者奥利弗骑着自行车穿过大教堂前的广场和老城小巷。导演瓜达尼诺就住在克雷马，电影上映后这里成了影迷打卡地
scene_en: the novel sets the story in a villa on the Italian coast in the 1980s; the film moves it to the summer of 1983 and to Crema in the Lombard plain, where Elio and Oliver, the American scholar staying with his family, cycle across the cathedral square and through the old streets. The director Luca Guadagnino lives in Crema, and fans have been coming ever since the film came out
